outcome: A case of Rosa's conjecture (Dutch windmills of any order with three pendant triangles are graceful or nearly-graceful) was settled by Alkasasbeh, Dyer and Shalaby using Skolem-type sequences, but the underlying mathematical result was first posted to arXiv in June 2020 (revised August 2021) and only appeared in a journal (Australasian Journal of Combinatorics 91(2), 2025) after the frozen revision date; no result actually occurring inside the 26 Jan 2024 - present window was found, and the general conjecture remains open.
summary: The triage's found item — 'Applying Skolem Sequences to Gracefully Label New Families of Triangular Windmills' (Alkasasbeh, Dyer, Shalaby), which the triage saw published in Australasian Journal of Combinatorics 91(2) (2025), pp. 242-265 — is the same paper as arXiv:2006.16396, first submitted 29 June 2020 and revised 9 August 2021 (confirmed via WebFetch on the arXiv abstract page, which shows [v1] 2020 and [v2] 2021). The paper proves that any Dutch windmill with three pendant triangles (a family of triangular cacti, i.e. connected graphs whose blocks are all triangles) is graceful or near-graceful depending on its residue mod 4, settling a case (not the whole) of Rosa's conjecture, via Skolem-type/Langford sequence constructions across eleven sub-types. This is a genuine case of the parent problem under §3.1 (a restriction to a specific sub-family of triangular cacti, not a variant), so if the result had appeared inside the window it would be classified 'partial'. But the mathematics itself long predates the 26 January 2024 frozen revision — the AJC 'publication' in 2025 is only the journal's belated formal print of a five-year-old arXiv preprint, a lag explicitly anticipated by §6.1's rationale for 'open_stale' and by §6.3's instruction to date by the first written argument rather than the journal date. I found no other paper, preprint, or announcement addressing Rosa's conjecture (or any triangular-cacti sub-case of it) with a first-written-argument date after 26 January 2024; a November 2025 arXiv paper ('On the gracesize of trees', arXiv:2511.11331) addresses the sibling graceful tree conjecture (an approximate/asymptotic version for trees), not Rosa's conjecture on triangular cacti, and is a different problem in this dataset's terms. No source anywhere mentions AI, machine learning, automated theorem proving, or computational search in connection with this paper or with Rosa's conjecture generally — the method is classical combinatorial construction (Skolem/Langford sequences) by hand. Confidence is high that nothing happened to this specific problem inside the window, though I could not fully render the two PDFs' raw text (WebFetch reported binary/compressed content for both ajc_v91_p242.pdf and a related Memorial University thesis PDF) and instead relied on the arXiv abstract page, ResearchGate listing, and multiple independent search-engine summaries, all of which agree on authorship, dates, and content.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2025 AJC publication itself is the 'event' that counts, on the theory that the paper was not authoritative/expert-vetted mathematics until it passed peer review and appeared in a journal of record, and that the 2020 arXiv posting was merely a claim. Under that reading the status would be 'partial' with event date 2025 (journal) and the case would count as in-window progress. I reject this reading because §6.3 explicitly instructs dating by the first written argument, precisely to prevent journal lag from moving results across the window boundary, and because there is no evidence the mathematical content changed between the 2021 arXiv v2 and the 2025 journal version — this looks like an ordinary long peer-review queue, not new work.
what_would_settle_it: A diff between arXiv v2 (2021) and the published AJC version would confirm whether the journal version added any new mathematical content after 26 January 2024 (e.g. an additional family of cacti, a strengthened bound); if it did, that increment would be a genuine in-window 'partial' result dated to the journal publication.
